sub_questions: What is the current research frontier (as of 2026) in confidence/calibration/uncertainty estimation for code LLMs, and which papers define it?
What are the specific caveats, holes, unproven claims, and open problems in that frontier that a new paper could occupy?
Where is the current 'calibration-disconnect' manuscript weak or merely diagnostic, and what positive/prescriptive extension would raise it to AAAI-27 main-track novelty?
Which ~5-10 papers are load-bearing for the chosen direction, and what does each contribute or leave open?
What is the single most novel headline claim available, and exactly which experiment(s) produce the headline number?
Why is that headline likely to come out favorable given ONLY single-GPU 7B-scale compute (feasibility + prior-evidence grounding)?
What supporting results are needed to make the headline defensible, and what is the most likely failure mode plus a pre-registered fallback?

How does the proposal defend novelty against the closest existing work (Spiess ICSE'25, Campos multicalibration, Stangel Rewarding Doubt, UQ4CT, semantic-entropy/self-consistency line, selective generation/abstention)?

Which single AAAI-27 primary topic/keyword (verbatim from the areas-and-topics list) best fits the proposed paper under AAAI's own selection rules, and what 1-2 secondary keywords, such that the paper's main methodological contribution sits squarely in that subarea and never drifts out of scope?

entities.name: Selective generation / abstention / deferral for code

required_formats: shortlist of ~5-10 papers with per-paper hole/contribution
scored comparison of 2-4 candidate paper directions on (novelty, confidence)
one committed paper proposal with a single headline claim
required_sections: ## Headline Claim and the Experiment That Produces It
## Why the Headline Will Likely Land (feasibility + prior evidence)
## Novelty Defense vs. Closest Prior Work
required_section_headings: ## 1. The Research Frontier in Code-LLM Confidence and Calibration
## 2. Caveats, Holes, and Open Problems at the Frontier
## 3. Where the Current Calibration-Disconnect Paper Falls Short of Main-Track
## 4. Candidate Directions, Scored on Novelty and Confidence
## 6. Headline Claim and the Exact Experiment That Produces It
## 7. Why the Headline Will Likely Land: Feasibility on Single-GPU 7B Compute
## 8. Supporting Results, Failure Mode, and Pre-Registered Fallback
## 9. Novelty Defense Against the Closest Prior Work
## 10. AAAI-27 Topic Alignment: Primary and Secondary Keywords
scope_conditions: single-GPU 7B-scale compute only (A100-40GB / GH200 98GB); no multi-node or frontier-scale training
priority 1 = novelty, priority 2 = confidence in attaining headline + supporting results (binding rank order)
the deliverable is a paper PROPOSAL, not a survey; exactly ONE final idea
must extend the existing calibration-disconnect code-LLM paper, not start an unrelated topic
MUST pin to one AAAI-27 primary topic/keyword (verbatim from areas-and-topics list) and never deviate from that scope; contribution must be METHODOLOGICAL (main-track), not application/measurement
must fit AAAI-27 format: 7 pages main content (max 9 total), reproducibility checklist; scope to ONE tight headline story
